channel.title: Efficient Training
channel.description: Technical notes by Jaehun Ryu, a deep learning compiler engineer, on LLM inference, KV caches, compilers, C++, AI papers, and open-source code.

item.title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
item.description:
Paper

Introduction

Blackwell GPUs execute FP8 and FP4 matrix multiplies 2x and 4x faster than BF16, respectively. To bring that speed to attention, the first problem to solve is not precision loss but whether “a quantized value is reconstructed identically in the forward and backward computations.” FLAMIA designs this condition inside a low-bit attention kernel and turns it into training calls that are actually faster on Blackwell.

item.title: SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding
item.description:
Paper

SpecOPD: Training Speculative Decoding Drafters with Branch Parallelism

Introduction

Speculative decoding speeds up generation by having a small drafter propose multiple tokens that a large target verifies in a single pass. But the ceiling on that speed is set by how many tokens the drafter can get right in a row, and on-policy distillation, the approach aimed at this problem, is tied to sequential draft-verify rollouts while collecting its training signal. SpecOPD starts from the observation that this sequential dependence is not essential to on-policy learning.

item.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention
item.description:
Training on long documents across several GPUs creates more than a compute problem. Each GPU also needs the right attention mask: the rules that determine which tokens may attend to which other tokens. If those rules leave one GPU with more work than the others, the entire training step waits for it.

FlashMask-3 starts with how masks are stored, then uses that representation to select work, distribute it, and overlap communication with computation. The paper reports a 7.3–11.0% improvement in full training throughput for a MoE model with a 128K context on 128 H100 GPUs. That result must be distinguished from the speedup of the attention kernel alone (§4.3, Table 1).

item.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
item.description:
Paper

TL;DR

In looped language models, the state converges to a fixed point $z^\star = F_\theta(z^\star; x)$ as the recursion depth grows, and near the fixed point the “endpoint” can stand in for the entire trajectory. This paper uses that one property to reduce four different costs at once across pretraining, serving, and RL: (1) training backpropagates only through the last $b$ recursions (truncated BPTT), (2) decoding caches only the last KV bank for each token (terminal KV sharing, a $3\times$ cut in cache), (3) prefill is distilled into a lightweight student that predicts the fixed point directly, giving up to a $1.79\times$ speedup, and (4) RL reuses gradients from stored rollout states to make updates $2\times$ faster. It also improves the two devices that actually produce this fixed point — the depth prior and input injection — as a “learned prior” and “orthogonal injection (OrthoInj)” respectively, lowering perplexity across the whole range from 100M to 1.6B parameters (source: §1).

item.title: On-Policy or Off-Policy Learning? A Systematic Study of Distillation Dynamics
item.description:
On-Policy Is Not a Panacea: The Real Protagonists of Rollout Policy, KL Direction, and Learning Rate in Distillation Dynamics

TL;DR — When we separate on-policy (OnPD) and off-policy (OffPD) distillation in strong-to-weak distillation, what determines final performance, forgetting, and update sparsity is not the rollout policy but the KL direction and the learning rate. Forward KL is surprisingly robust to the rollout policy, reverse KL is sensitive, and forgetting and update sparsity are essentially entirely decided by the learning rate.

item.title: MassAlloc Attention: Let Attention Allocate Its Own Compute
item.description:
Paper

MassAlloc Attention (MALA): Letting Attention Allocate Its Own Compute

TL;DR — Full softmax attention (FullAttn) performs all post-score computation after QK score generation for every causal tile, whereas MALA uses the normalized mass produced by attention itself to selectively perform post-score operations. As a result, it maintains FullAttn-level quality while reducing training forward/backward latency by $2.2\times$ / $3.0\times$ and decoding latency by $1.6\times$, and cuts total training FLOPs by $23.1\%$ in 32K long-context training of a 14B model (source: Abstract, §3).

item.title: ZGCM-1: A Fully Open and Extremely Efficient Foundation Model for Math and Agentic Search
item.description:
Paper

ZGCM-1: How a 7B Dense Model Trades Blows with 235B Frontiers — A Fully Open, Ultra-Efficient Foundation Model Design Report

TL;DR — With a single 7.39B dense model, ZGCM-1 scores 75.0% on AIME 2026, 63.1% on WebWalkerQA, and 62.0% on Binary Function Search, breaking the conventional wisdom that “frontier reasoning is the exclusive province of tens of billions of parameters.” The secret is not inflating parameters but a fully open recipe built on a hybrid architecture of gated sliding-window attention + global attention that cuts the KV cache by 6.4×, FP8 + Muon + TWEO that shortens pretraining by roughly 4.2×, and MDP mid-training that learns 256K long contexts.

item.title: Miles v0.1: Production-Level Post-Training
item.description:
Paper

Miles v0.1: A “verified, clean, and scalable” full-stack system for frontier RL post-training

TL;DR: Miles is a full-stack RL post-training framework that resolves the train-rollout mismatch at the system level — the mismatch that arises when rollout generation and training run on different engines, kernels, and precisions. It unifies SGLang-based rollout, a Megatron-LM/FSDP trainer, and three weight-synchronization transports (broadcast/P2P/disk-delta), while also guaranteeing token exactness (TITO) and expert-routing replay (R3). As an end-to-end case study, it trains GLM-5.2 744B-A40B on 64 GB300 GPUs with fully asynchronous agentic RL, achieving a median step time of 263 seconds (source: §9.2, Fig. 5).

item.title: Online Draft Co-Training for Speculative Decoding in Large-Scale, Long-Context RL Post-Training
item.description:
Paper

Two Designs That Make Speculative Decoding Practical for Large-Scale, Long-Context RL Post-Training

TL;DR : Rollout generation dominates the wall-clock time of RL post-training. This work accelerates it with speculative decoding, and adds online draft co-training so the draft does not lag behind as the policy evolves. However, existing systems fail to handle the branch attention used by advanced drafts (unsupported by context parallelism) and target features scattered across stages (a pipeline parallelism problem). This paper proposes (1) a CP technique that decomposes branch attention into a causal main-sequence component and a rank-local branch and merges them, and (2) TapChannel, which delivers target features outside the pipeline schedule, achieving 1.16–1.88× end-to-end speedup from 8B to 122B (source: §3.3, Tab. 1).

item.title: [Paper Review] Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
item.description:
Paper Link

Structured State Space Duality: Unifying SSMs and Attention with Mamba-2 for 2–8× Acceleration

TL;DR

Structured State-Space Duality (SSD) reveals that SSMs and masked attention compute the same function with different contraction orders. It introduces a matmul-dominant kernel based on block decomposition and low-rank properties, achieving 2–8× speedup over Mamba-scan and outperforming FlashAttention-2 for sequences longer than 2k tokens. In a 2.7B / 300B tokens pre-training setup, it matches the quality of Transformer++ and shows further improvement to a PPL of 5.95 when mixed with 6 attention layers (Source: Abstract, Fig. 10, Tab. 3, §9.2–9.3).

item.title: Janus-Pro: Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Data and Model Scaling
item.description:
Paper

Janus-Pro 7B: Dual-Encoder Multimodal LLM That Outsmarts Bigger Models

One-line summary (TL;DR)

By fully separating the SigLIP understanding encoder from the VQ generation encoder and attaching them to a 7 B-parameter LLM with a ‘Dual-Encoder + Adapter’ design, it becomes the first case to beat a 13 B unified model (TokenFlow-XL) on both understanding and generation at the same time. – MMBench 79.2 (+10.3 pt) / GenEval 0.80 (+45 %)
